questions.question: Which EC2 pricing model requires no upfront payment and no long-term commitment?

explanation.correct: On-Demand instances require no commitment and no upfront payment — you pay per second or per hour only while the instance is running.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans require a 1 or 3-year commitment. Spot Instances have no commitment but carry interruption risk.

questions.question: What is the maximum discount available with Spot Instances compared to On-Demand?

explanation.correct: Spot Instances can provide up to 90% discount compared to On-Demand pricing — the highest of all five pricing models.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances offer up to 72%, Savings Plans up to 66–72%. Spot offers the most because it comes with interruption risk.

questions.question: What is the maximum discount available with Reserved Instances?

explanation.correct: Reserved Instances offer up to 72% discount compared to On-Demand when you choose a 3-year All Upfront commitment.
explanation.why: 72% is for 3-year All Upfront Standard RI. Savings Plans Compute SP is up to 66%. Spot is up to 90% but comes with interruption risk.

questions.question: Which EC2 pricing model is most suitable for a fault-tolerant batch processing workload?

explanation.correct: Spot Instances are ideal for fault-tolerant batch workloads because they offer the highest discount (up to 90%) and the workload can restart after interruption.
explanation.why: On-Demand is expensive. Reserved requires commitment. Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive and are for compliance/licensing needs.

questions.question: How much notice does AWS give before terminating a Spot Instance?

explanation.correct: AWS provides a 2-minute interruption warning before terminating a Spot Instance. This can be detected via instance metadata or Amazon EventBridge.
explanation.why: The 2-minute warning is a fixed AWS specification and is a critical exam fact for Spot Instance interruption handling.

questions.question: Which Reserved Instance type allows you to change the instance family during the commitment period?

explanation.correct: Convertible Reserved Instances allow you to exchange for a different instance family, OS, or tenancy — but provide a lower discount than Standard RIs.
explanation.why: Standard RIs are locked to the original instance family. Zonal and Regional describe RI scope, not type. Scheduled RIs are for specific time windows.

questions.question: Which pricing model provides a capacity reservation guarantee in a specific Availability Zone?

explanation.correct: Zonal Reserved Instances provide a capacity reservation in the specific AZ — AWS guarantees your instances will launch even during peak demand.
explanation.why: Regional RIs provide a discount across the region but do not guarantee capacity in a specific AZ. Savings Plans and On-Demand do not provide capacity reservations.

questions.question: What is the primary reason a company would choose Dedicated Hosts over other EC2 pricing models?

options.text: To get the highest discount on compute costs
For compliance requirements and Bring Your Own License (BYOL) support
To get the fastest instance launch times

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts are used for compliance requirements (hardware isolation) and BYOL software licensing (Microsoft, Oracle) that requires visibility into physical socket/core counts.
explanation.why: Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive model — not used for cost savings. Auto Scaling and launch speed are unrelated to Dedicated Hosts.

questions.question: Linux On-Demand EC2 instances are billed in what increment?

explanation.correct: Linux and macOS On-Demand instances are billed per second with a minimum of 60 seconds. Windows instances are billed per hour.
explanation.why: Per-second billing means you only pay for exactly what you use. Windows still uses hourly billing.

questions.question: Which Savings Plans type provides the most flexibility, applying to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda?

explanation.correct: Compute Savings Plans automatically apply to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage regardless of instance family, size, region, or OS — offering up to 66% discount.
explanation.why: EC2 Instance Savings Plans are locked to one instance family per region. SageMaker SP applies only to SageMaker. 'Reserved Savings Plan' is not a real AWS product.

questions.question: A company has Standard Reserved Instances for m5.xlarge but wants to switch to c5.xlarge. What problem do they face?

options.text: They cannot change the region of a Reserved Instance
Standard RIs cannot be exchanged for a different instance family
Reserved Instances cannot be used with Linux
They must pay a penalty fee for early termination

explanation.correct: Standard Reserved Instances are locked to the original instance family. To change families, you need Convertible RIs or must sell the Standard RI on the Reserved Instance Marketplace.
explanation.why: Region changes are not possible for any RI. There is no early termination penalty for RIs — you simply stop getting the discount benefit.

questions.question: Which of the following workloads is LEAST suitable for Spot Instances?

options.text: Machine learning model training with checkpointing

explanation.correct: Production databases cannot tolerate the 2-minute interruption warning of Spot Instances — abrupt termination risks data corruption and service outage.
explanation.why: Batch, ML with checkpointing, and rendering are all fault-tolerant workloads that can restart after interruption — ideal for Spot.

questions.question: A company commits to spending $0.10 per hour on compute for 3 years. Which pricing model are they using?

explanation.correct: Savings Plans are commitment-based on a minimum hourly spend (dollars per hour), not on a specific instance type. This is the key distinction from Reserved Instances.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances commit to a specific instance configuration. On-Demand has no commitment. Dedicated Hosts commit to a physical server.

questions.question: What is the key difference between Dedicated Instances and Dedicated Hosts?

options.text: Dedicated Instances are cheaper; Dedicated Hosts are more expensive
Dedicated Hosts provide visibility into socket/core count and BYOL support; Dedicated Instances only provide hardware isolation from other accounts
Dedicated Instances support BYOL; Dedicated Hosts do not
There is no difference — they are the same product with different names

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts give you an entire physical server with socket/core visibility (required for per-socket/per-core BYOL licenses). Dedicated Instances just ensure no other AWS account shares your hardware, but you cannot see physical hardware details.
explanation.why: Both provide hardware isolation, but only Dedicated Hosts support BYOL and give you hardware-level control. They are not the same product.

questions.question: A company runs a web application that needs exactly 10 instances during business hours (8 AM–8 PM) and 0 instances at night. Which Reserved Instance type was designed for this use case?

explanation.correct: Scheduled Reserved Instances allow you to reserve capacity for specific recurring time windows (e.g., daily 8 AM–8 PM) at a lower price than On-Demand.
explanation.why: Standard and Convertible RIs apply 24/7. Zonal describes scope (AZ-level), not timing. Scheduled RIs are purpose-built for predictable time-window workloads.

questions.question: A startup uses a mix of On-Demand instances for their baseline load, Spot Instances for burst capacity, and Reserved Instances for their minimum guaranteed capacity. What strategy is this called?

explanation.correct: The mixed fleet strategy combines Reserved Instances (baseline), On-Demand (moderate spikes), and Spot (burst/peak) to maximise cost efficiency at every tier of demand.
explanation.why: Auto Scaling is a service for automatic instance management. Capacity reservation is a specific EC2 feature. Hybrid cloud refers to on-premises + cloud, not pricing models.

questions.question: Which payment option for Reserved Instances provides the maximum discount?

explanation.correct: All Upfront payment for Reserved Instances provides the highest discount because AWS receives the full payment immediately, reducing their financial risk.
explanation.why: No Upfront and Partial Upfront provide smaller discounts. 'Monthly billing' is not a separate RI payment option — No Upfront is billed monthly.

questions.question: A company has unused Standard Reserved Instances they no longer need. What can they do?

options.text: Sell them on the Reserved Instance Marketplace
Transfer them to another AWS region
Return them to AWS for a full refund

explanation.correct: AWS provides the Reserved Instance Marketplace where customers can sell unused Standard Reserved Instances to other AWS customers.
explanation.why: RIs cannot be converted to Spot Instances. RIs are region-specific and cannot be transferred across regions. AWS does not offer refunds for unused RIs.

questions.question: What does 'horizontal scaling' mean in the context of EC2 pricing?

options.text: Resizing an instance to a larger type
Adding more instances of the same type
Increasing storage capacity of an instance
Moving instances to a different region

explanation.correct: Horizontal scaling (scale out) means adding more instances of the same type. Each new instance is billed independently at its own rate.
explanation.why: Resizing to a larger type is vertical scaling (scale up). Storage changes are independent of compute pricing. Region changes are migrations.

questions.question: A Compute Savings Plan is purchased for $0.10/hr. The company's actual EC2+Fargate+Lambda spend is $0.15/hr. How is the billing handled?

options.text: The full $0.15 is covered by the Savings Plan at the discounted rate
The first $0.10 is billed at the Savings Plan discount rate; the remaining $0.05 is billed at On-Demand rates
The Savings Plan is invalid because the actual spend exceeds the commitment
AWS rounds the commitment up to cover the full $0.15

explanation.correct: Savings Plans cover compute usage up to the committed amount at the discounted rate. Any usage beyond the commitment is billed at standard On-Demand rates automatically.
explanation.why: Savings Plans don't provide a blanket discount on all usage — only on usage within the committed hourly spend. Excess usage is On-Demand.

questions.question: Which service allows you to view recommendations for Reserved Instances or Savings Plans based on your actual AWS usage history?

explanation.correct: AWS Cost Explorer analyses your historical usage patterns and provides automated recommendations for which Reserved Instances or Savings Plans would provide the best savings for your specific workload.
explanation.why: CloudTrail is for API auditing. AWS Config is for resource compliance. Trusted Advisor provides general best practice checks but Cost Explorer provides specific RI/SP recommendations.

questions.question: A company needs to run a database with a Microsoft SQL Server license they already own. The license is per physical socket. Which EC2 option should they choose?

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts provide visibility into the physical socket count and are the only EC2 option that supports Bring Your Own License (BYOL) for per-socket or per-core licensed software like SQL Server.
explanation.why: Dedicated Instances only isolate hardware — they don't expose socket/core details needed for BYOL licensing. On-Demand and Standard RIs run on shared hardware.

questions.question: Which Spot Instance feature allows you to maintain a collection of Spot Instances across multiple types and AZs to reduce interruption risk?

explanation.correct: Spot Fleet lets you define a target capacity and AWS fulfils it by intelligently combining multiple instance types and AZs using a diversified allocation strategy, reducing the likelihood of all instances being interrupted at once.
explanation.why: 'Spot Reserve', 'Spot Diversity Group', and 'Spot Cluster' are not real AWS features. Spot Fleet is the actual managed collection feature for Spot Instances.

questions.question: A team uses t3.micro On-Demand instances for development. They are within the 12-month free tier. How are these instances billed?

options.text: At full On-Demand rates from the first instance
Free up to 750 hours per month; On-Demand rates beyond that
Free for any number of hours during the free tier period
At 50% of the On-Demand rate during free tier

explanation.correct: The AWS Free Tier provides 750 hours per month of t2.micro or t3.micro On-Demand instances for the first 12 months. Usage beyond 750 hours is billed at normal On-Demand rates.
explanation.why: 750 hours equals approximately one full month for a single instance (744 hours). Two instances running simultaneously would consume the free tier in ~15 days.

questions.question: An organisation has a legally mandated requirement that its financial workloads must not share underlying hardware with any other company. The compliance team also wants detailed reports showing which physical hardware runs each workload. What is the correct solution?

options.text: Use Dedicated Instances with Reserved pricing
Use On-Demand instances in a dedicated VPC
Use Spot Instances in an isolated subnet

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts provide both hardware isolation from other AWS accounts AND full visibility into the physical host details (host ID, socket count, core count) needed for compliance reports. Dedicated Instances provide isolation but lack the physical hardware visibility.
explanation.why: Dedicated Instances don't provide hardware-level reporting. A dedicated VPC is a network isolation concept, not hardware isolation. Spot Instances run on shared hardware.

questions.question: A company's EC2 fleet currently uses Standard Reserved Instances for m5.2xlarge. Their architecture team decides to migrate to Graviton-based m6g.2xlarge instances for a 20% performance improvement and lower cost. What is the challenge with their current RIs?

options.text: Graviton instances cannot use Reserved Instances
Standard RIs cannot change instance family — m5 and m6g are different families
Reserved Instances cannot be used across different regions
Reserved Instances only apply to x86 instances and are invalid for ARM

explanation.correct: Standard Reserved Instances are locked to the original instance family. m5 (Intel x86) and m6g (AWS Graviton ARM) are different families. To migrate, the company would need Convertible RIs (exchangeable) or sell Standard RIs on the Marketplace and buy new ones.
explanation.why: Graviton instances fully support Reserved Instances and Savings Plans. The constraint is specifically about Standard RI inflexibility — not about Graviton compatibility.

questions.question: A company's production workload has a stable baseline of 20 instances running 24/7 and occasional spikes to 50 instances for 2–3 days during month-end processing. What is the most cost-optimal pricing strategy?

options.text: 20 Reserved Instances for baseline + On-Demand or Spot for the spike of 30 instances

explanation.correct: The mixed fleet strategy: 20 Reserved Instances cover the stable baseline at maximum discount. The 30-instance spike (only 2–3 days/month) is served by On-Demand or Spot — committing to 50 Reserved Instances wastes money the other 27–28 days when only 20 are needed.
explanation.why: Option A is the most expensive. Option B wastes 30 reserved slots most of the month. Option D risks interruption of production workloads. Option C is optimal.

questions.question: A Data Engineering team runs ML training jobs that take 8–12 hours. Jobs use checkpointing every 30 minutes. They want to minimise cost. Which combination is most appropriate?

options.text: Spot Instances — up to 90% savings, job can resume from last checkpoint if interrupted
Dedicated Hosts — best performance for ML workloads

explanation.correct: The checkpointing every 30 minutes makes the ML job fault-tolerant — worst case, a Spot interruption means re-running at most 30 minutes of work. The 90% discount over On-Demand makes this highly cost-efficient for long training jobs.
explanation.why: On-Demand is reliable but expensive. Reserved requires a 1-year commitment for sporadic training jobs. Dedicated Hosts are for compliance/BYOL, not ML cost optimisation.

questions.question: An enterprise runs 100 EC2 instances of various types across multiple regions. Their compute needs change frequently as they adopt new services. They want predictable savings similar to Reserved Instances but with maximum flexibility. What is the best solution?

options.text: Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for each instance type
Purchase Convertible Reserved Instances for each instance type

explanation.correct: Compute Savings Plans provide RI-level savings (up to 66%) with complete flexibility — they automatically apply to any EC2 instance family, size, region, OS, and even Fargate and Lambda. Perfect for dynamic environments where instance mix changes frequently.
explanation.why: Standard RIs lock you to a specific configuration. Convertible RIs allow changes but require manual exchange requests. On-Demand offers no savings.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the Spot Instance Advisor tool provided by AWS?

options.text: A tool that automatically bids for Spot Instances on your behalf
A tool that shows the historical interruption frequency and discount percentage for Spot Instances by type and region
A tool that recommends which EC2 pricing model to use based on your usage history
A service that guarantees Spot Instances will not be interrupted for a minimum of 1 hour

explanation.correct: The Spot Instance Advisor shows historical interruption rates (as < 5%, 5–10%, etc.) and current discount vs On-Demand for each instance type per region — helping you choose instance types with low interruption rates.
explanation.why: AWS does not bid on your behalf automatically. Cost Explorer handles pricing model recommendations. No AWS service guarantees Spot Instance availability — that would contradict the Spot model.

questions.question: A company purchases a 1-year, No Upfront, Standard Reserved Instance for t3.large in us-east-1. Three months later, the application is migrated to us-west-2. What happens to the RI?

options.text: The RI automatically transfers to us-west-2
The RI continues to apply to any t3.large instance in us-east-1; the company pays On-Demand for us-west-2
AWS refunds the unused portion of the RI

explanation.correct: Reserved Instances are region-specific. The RI continues to apply billing discounts to any qualifying t3.large instance in us-east-1. If no instance is running there, the RI is wasted. The company can sell it on the RI Marketplace to recoup some value.
explanation.why: RIs don't transfer across regions automatically. AWS does not cancel or refund RIs. The discount simply applies to matching usage in the original region.

questions.question: What is the minimum billing duration for a Linux Spot Instance?

explanation.correct: Linux Spot Instances are billed per second with a minimum of 60 seconds (1 minute), the same as On-Demand Linux instances.
explanation.why: This means if a Spot Instance is terminated in under 60 seconds, you are still billed for the full first minute. After the first minute, billing is per second.

questions.question: A financial services company needs to run workloads on isolated hardware and use their existing Oracle licenses (priced per physical core). They also want a discount for long-term usage. What should they choose?

options.text: On-Demand instances in an isolated VPC

explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts are required for BYOL Oracle licensing (per-core). Purchasing Dedicated Hosts with a 3-year reservation provides a significant discount over On-Demand Dedicated Host pricing while meeting the compliance and licensing requirements.
explanation.why: Dedicated Instances don't support per-core BYOL. Standard RIs run on shared hardware. An isolated VPC provides network isolation, not hardware isolation.
